#### SND@LHC prepares an all-silicon upgrade for the high-luminosity LHC

[CERN announced on 13 November](https://home.cern/sndlhc-experiment-set-to-push-the-neutrino-frontier/) that SND@LHC will replace its nuclear-emulsion target with a fully electronic detector for high-luminosity LHC running. The experiment sits about **480 m downstream of ATLAS** and recorded Run 3 data from July 2022 through June 2026. Its upgrade will reuse **1,680 silicon-microstrip modules** removed from the CMS outer tracker; a prototype is now in beam tests. Real-time readout will replace the integrated exposure delivered by emulsions, which cannot tolerate the future particle flux, although the silicon system has coarser intrinsic position resolution.

The design also includes a magnet intended to distinguish neutrino from antineutrino interactions. CERN identifies direct detection of the tau antineutrino as a central target: it is the remaining Standard Model particle whose interaction has not been observed directly. This is a detector-development milestone, not a tau-antineutrino observation or a demonstrated sensitivity. CERN did not publish a complete construction schedule, exposure forecast or expected event yield in the announcement.

#### A compact high-rate quantum code gets a fault-tolerant encoder

Naoyuki Kanomata and Hayato Goto report a fault-tolerant state-preparation method for a symplectic-double quantum code in a [peer-reviewed *Science Advances* paper published 13 November](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aec4142). The code encodes **six logical qubits in 30 physical qubits**. According to the [RIKEN and JST technical announcement dated 14 November](https://www.jst.go.jp/pr/announce/20261114/index.html), the new all-plus-state circuit reduces the number of CNOT gates from **108 to 67** and adds a procedure for detecting damaging faults during encoding.

Numerical simulations reported by the team retain a logical error rate comparable to the earlier construction while reducing the total number of required physical qubits by more than half; the authors also construct arbitrary-state encoding for all six logical qubits. The advance addresses preparation overhead for a specific high-rate code. It is a design and simulation result, not an experimental demonstration of logical qubits, and its practical value will depend on hardware connectivity, gate errors, syndrome extraction and the cost of the remaining fault-tolerant operations.

#### A metal-organic framework creates a sharply polarized triplet radical pair

A [peer-reviewed *Nature Communications* study published 13 November](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-79262-6) places porphyrin electron donors and naphthalene-diimide acceptors roughly **10 Å** apart in a metal-organic framework. Transient spectroscopy gives charge separation on a **33 ps** timescale, much faster than the approximately **1.8 ns** intersystem-crossing pathway in the control system. The apparent charge-separation yield is close to **0.98**, but the authors estimate that the long-lived triplet charge-separated population is only about **0.1%**, corresponding to roughly **1.6 × 10⁻³ spins per pore**.

Electron-paramagnetic-resonance measurements show selective population of the triplet radical pair's T0 sublevel, with relaxation that changes when guest solvents occupy the pores. This gives a chemically tunable route to spin hyperpolarization in a crystalline scaffold. The work does not demonstrate long transverse coherence, quantum sensing or transfer of polarization to an analyte; those are potential applications rather than measured capabilities.

#### An end-to-end neural system forecasts the eddy-resolving global ocean

Xiang Zhang and colleagues present WenHai-E2E in a [peer-reviewed *Science Advances* article published 13 November](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aeh9058). Unlike many machine-learning ocean models that still require initial conditions from an operational numerical forecast, the system ingests multisource ocean observations and produces a global eddy-resolving forecast without that numerical initialization pipeline. The publisher-indexed abstract reports higher forecast accuracy than a state-of-the-art numerical global ocean forecast system.

The architecture is scientifically relevant because the initialization step is a major barrier to independent deployment of data-driven ocean forecasts. **Evidence access:** the article page was inaccessible at the cutoff, so only the bibliographic record and abstract were reviewed; no unverified skill score, resolution, lead time or compute-saving factor is quoted here. Performance on the authors' test distribution is not yet evidence of operational robustness under sparse observations, regime shifts or extreme events, and the comparison needs the full methods and evaluation protocol for independent assessment.

#### High-precision krypton-81 dating reaches the Late Pleistocene radiocarbon overlap

A [peer-reviewed *Science Advances* study published 13 November](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aef6864) reports an Atom Trap Trace Analysis workflow that lowers the practical young-age boundary of krypton-81 groundwater dating from roughly **50,000 years to about 10,000 years**. In North China Plain samples, paired carbon-14 and krypton-81 ages agree for approximately **10–30 ka** after carbon-geochemical correction; older samples retain an absolute krypton clock after radiocarbon corrections become increasingly uncertain. The dual tracer also helps identify mixed groundwater, and the screened oxygen-isotope sequence is consistent with polar-ice palaeoclimate records.

Krypton-81 is chemically inert and has a half-life of about **229,000 years**, so the improved atom counting closes a useful gap between radiocarbon and conventional krypton dating. **Evidence access:** the quantitative claims above come from the indexed abstract; the full article could not be retrieved at the cutoff. The demonstration is in one aquifer system, and age interpretation still depends on sampling, mixing and the atmospheric isotope baseline. The result extends an analytical method; it does not make every old groundwater sample uniquely dateable.

#### Reconstructed mountain-belt thickness rises in two deep-time steps

Matthijs Smit and colleagues compiled metamorphic peak pressures over the past **3 billion years** to infer maximum crustal thickness in a [peer-reviewed *Science Advances* paper published 13 November](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aei2764). Their reconstruction shows two broad increases: from roughly **30 to 60 km** around 2.7–2.2 billion years ago, and from roughly **60 to 90 km** around 0.8–0.7 billion years ago. The timing overlaps changes in terrigenous element delivery, sulfur metabolism and surface oxygenation.

The proposed mechanism is that taller, more extensive mountain belts exposed more rock to weathering and erosion, increasing nutrient flux and helping alter ocean-atmosphere chemistry. The [UBC research summary published 13 November](https://www.eoas.ubc.ca/news/1794603471) correctly presents this as a mechanistic proposal. Correlation across coarse geological timescales does not establish that mountain growth caused oxygenation or biological diversification. Maximum preserved pressure is also an indirect proxy for mountain-belt height and is vulnerable to preservation, sampling and tectonic-model assumptions.

#### Enhancer-targeted CRISPR activation rescues cellular phenotypes in autism-gene models

A [peer-reviewed, open-access *Nature Neuroscience* study published 13 November](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41593-026-02504-9) maps regulatory enhancers for *CHD8* and *SCN2A*, two genes in which loss of one functional copy can cause neurodevelopmental disorders. The researchers used dCas9-p300 to activate selected enhancers of the remaining intact allele in human-pluripotent-stem-cell-derived excitatory neurons and cerebral forebrain organoids. Expression gains persisted for three to five months, depending on the construct.

Untreated *CHD8* mutant organoids showed **5,933 differentially expressed genes** relative to controls; enhancer activation shifted transcriptomes toward the control state and improved proliferation and maturation markers. In *SCN2A* models, treatment improved neuronal maturation and several intrinsic-excitability and action-potential measures, although resting membrane potential was not fully normalized. Organoid-to-organoid variability was substantial, and in one configuration only about a quarter of cells expressed the activator. This is preclinical cell and organoid evidence, not an autism treatment. Delivery to the developing human brain, dose control, off-target regulation, timing and long-term safety remain unresolved.

#### Tirzepatide produces large 72-week BMI reductions in an adolescent trial

The phase 3 SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS trial was [published online in *JAMA* on 15 November](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2856796). It randomized **160 participants aged 12 to under 18** with obesity, or overweight plus an obesity-related complication, in a 2:1 ratio to once-weekly tirzepatide or placebo alongside lifestyle intervention. At 72 weeks, mean BMI changed by **−18.5%** with tirzepatide and **+0.5%** with placebo, a treatment difference of **−19.0 percentage points** (95% CI, −23.9 to −14.1; P < .001). At least 5% BMI reduction occurred in **79.6% versus 28.5%** of participants.

Gastrointestinal adverse events occurred in **81.5%** of the treatment group and **54.9%** of placebo recipients; **9.3%** receiving tirzepatide discontinued because of adverse events, compared with none receiving placebo. Serious adverse events occurred in 7.4% and 3.9%, respectively, and no deaths were reported. The sponsor-supported trial is small and lasts 72 weeks, has limited racial and ethnic diversity, and includes very few participants with type 2 diabetes or merely overweight. It establishes efficacy over the trial period; it does not resolve durability after stopping treatment, rare harms, effects on growth and maturation, or general effectiveness in routine adolescent care.

#### A tau fragment distinguishes mixed 3R/4R pathology in a small autopsy-linked cohort

A [peer-reviewed *JAMA* study published online 13 November](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2856780) evaluated the fluid marker eMTBR-tau243 in **229 participants**, including cerebrospinal-fluid samples from 196 and plasma from 55. In autopsy-confirmed Alzheimer disease, median cerebrospinal-fluid concentration was **0.459 fmol/mL** (10 cases), compared with **0.002 fmol/mL** in 29 cognitively unimpaired participants and **0.015 fmol/mL** across 52 non-Alzheimer tauopathies. Among symptomatic *MAPT* mutation carriers, the six mixed 3-repeat/4-repeat cases had a median of **0.140 fmol/mL**, versus **0.004 fmol/mL** in 15 four-repeat cases (P = .001).

The result supports eMTBR-tau243 as a marker of mixed 3R/4R tau pathology and suggests possible value beyond Alzheimer disease. It is not a validated standalone diagnostic test: the rare-disease subgroups are very small, samples came from heterogeneous retrospective biobanks, plasma data were more limited, and biofluid-to-autopsy intervals were not systematically modeled. The paper also reports relevant intellectual-property and industry relationships, including a licensed MTBR-tau243 patent held by the authors' institution.
